content.title: About
content.content: Puerto Rican style seafood paella is a traditional dish that blends the Spanish technique of cooking rice with the bold flavors of the Caribbean. It features short‑grain rice, a mix of seafood (shrimp, mussels, squid), tomatoes, sweet bell pepper, onion, garlic, and spices such as adobo, cumin, and saffron, which give the dish its vivid color and rich taste.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The Puerto Rican version is often cooked in a single large paellera, allowing all flavors to meld together.
A signature “mojo” sauce made from tomatoes, peppers, and aromatic herbs is commonly added.
Seafood is typically sourced fresh from the Atlantic waters surrounding Puerto Rico.
Saffron, the most expensive spice in the world, is sometimes substituted with turmeric in this regional recipe to keep costs down.
The dish is frequently served with lime wedges and fresh cilantro for a bright, tangy finish.

items.title: High‑quality protein
items.content: Shrimp, mussels, and squid provide complete protein essential for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: Omega‑3 fatty acids
items.content: The seafood contributes omega‑3s that support heart and vascular health.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Tomatoes, peppers, and onions supply B6, niacin, and folate, important for metabolism.

items.title: Antioxidants
items.content: Saffron (or turmeric) and tomatoes contain antioxidants that help combat free radicals.

items.title: Essential minerals
items.content: Seafood is rich in zinc, iron, and selenium, which bolster the immune system.

items.title: Seafood allergy
items.content: Individuals may experience allergic reactions to shrimp, mussels, or squid.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: Prepared adobo sauce can make the dish salty; adjust added salt accordingly.

items.title: Calorie density
items.content: With oil and rice, the dish can be calorie‑rich, so portion control is advised.

items.title: Heavy metal exposure
items.content: Some seafood may contain trace amounts of mercury; choose reputable sources.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the paella hot, often with lime wedges and fresh cilantro. Optional toppings include avocado slices or crunchy tortilla chips for added texture. It is typically eaten with a fork or wooden spoon.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store leftovers in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 2‑3 days. Reheat with a splash of broth or water to restore moisture. The paella can be frozen for up to 1 month, though the rice may become slightly drier.
